concerns.text: Task T031 (correlation calculation) and T030 (cross-architecture validation) depend on 'perplexity' or 'output entropy' data (FR-006) which is NOT produced by any preceding task. US-1 (T012) produces ground truth B*, US-2 (T020) produces static features. No task exists to run the separate greedy inference pass required to generate the 'independent measure of model uncertainty' (perplexity) needed for T031. This creates a consumer-before-producer violation where T031 cannot execute.

Task T027 explicitly notes a contradiction: Spec FR-003/US-3 requires 'regression models' (predicting continuous B*), but Plan.md and T027 itself mandate 'classification models' (predicting discrete classes). The task order assumes the classification path (T027, T029 using Accuracy/F1), but the spec requires regression (MAE/RMSE). This semantic dependency violation means the 'producer' (T027) emits artifacts (classification models) that do not satisfy the 'consumer' (T029/SC-001) requirements defined in the spec, breaking the data-flow contract.

Task T017 ('Perform feasibility mini-sweep') is placed AFTER T012-T016 (full sweep implementation). Logically, a feasibility check must precede the full implementation to validate the 6-hour CI assumption. While T017 is marked [US1], its execution order implies running the full sweep logic before validating it fits the time budget, violating the 'producer before consumer' logic of the CI constraint.
